title: Seeing touring shows, bands and TOBA acts in Pittsburgh
summary: As a girl she saw road shows, dance bands, Bessie Smith, Ma Rainey, the Elmore Theater and midnight shows.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: shows. We had Hot Chocolates and Black Birds to appear in Pittsburgh. So I mean, I got to see these productions when I was young.
And I remembered these things. And I remembered Adelaide, and I remembered all these artists who had --
The Broadway cast would actually go out on the road.
Of course, um hum.
And so therefore, I got a chance to see a lot of theater when I was young. There was the movies and --
Listen, we had bands come to Pittsburgh. You know, all the bands came there. As a youngster, I had been listening to music all my life when I was a kid.
My mother used to take me to the dance hall, because the bands --
I remember when they used to dance more or less in circles. You know, when a new dance would come out like the Fred Astaire and Adele Astaire popular dances would come out.
And people would line up and get there

partners and dance around in a circle rather than all over the floor, you know.
So I remember that as a kid -- going to dances and hearing bands.
And, of course, when Duke and Cab Calloway and Fats Waller was out on the road, you couldn't keep us away from the dance hall.
Although I liked to dance when I was younger, I usually wound up standing in front of the bandstand listening to the music.
And in this way, I got a chance to see everybody -- all of the performers.
And even in Pittsburgh, we had one of the TOBA theaters. And we saw all those acts, too.
Mamie Smith, Bessie Smith, Ma Rainey -- they played Pittsburgh.
We had a theater in Pittsburgh, the Elmore Theater, which all the black acts played there.
And then I had an uncle who took me downtown into Pittsburgh to catch a Wednesday matinee. They had the burlesque theaters -- I went with him to the burlesque houses and I saw a lot of acts, a lot of

burlesque.

And there were a lot of instances where there would be a black act on the burlesque circuit.

And then, there were productions that came out. They would have a midnight show and part of the performers would be all white performers -- you know, the white acts -- and then after that during the intermission, there would be the black acts to come on afterwards.

And that was a quite an experience for us, you know, who were out on the road.

And so we got a chance to see a lot of the popular comedians, vocalists, dancers -- tap dancers -- Bill Robinson.

Well, we saw everybody. So I've been exposed to it all my life.

In fact, somewhere along the line -- I mean, I don't know this to be true. I heard somewhere that my grandmother who was my father's mother from which that was the musical side of the family, that before they came to Homestead, that they had a little theater outside of Philadelphia called "The Spar Theater."
